newsitem.title: CROATIA: Bill volume rises at Croatia central bank auction.
newsitem.headline: Bill volume rises at Croatia central bank auction.

text.p: The volume of bills sold at Croatia's central bank primary bill auction on Wednesday rose to 167.5 million kuna from 118 million last week, as the banking sector enjoyed good liquidity throughout the week.
The accepted rates for 35- and 91-day liquidity bills were unchanged at 7.0 and 8.5 percent respectively. For the first time in months the bank sold its longest maturity 182-day bills at 9.5 percent.

Participation at primary sales of the central bank paper is limited to Croatia's banking sector, which uses these bills as collateral for Lombard loans, granted for a total of 12 working days each month.
A central bank official said Lombard loans rose on Wednesday to 25.2 million kuna from Tuesday's 14.2 million. -- Zagreb Newsroom +385 1 455 7075
